Seven things I still think about.

I did not have a case study to send you, so here is something else. Seven small moments that made me happy on a trip I took a couple of months ago, and what each one taught me about my own eye.

About

I have always loved brands. I just never called it a job.

Supermarket aisles, window shopping, reading about a brand before I have even tried it, all of that genuinely excites me, and it always has. I am not entirely sure how I ended up in change management at a bank instead of on a brand team, but somehow I still find my way back to noticing this stuff anyway.

Travel is where all of that comes alive for me even more. I love the whole process, researching a place properly before I get there, building an itinerary down to the smaller details, packing with an actual system, and then arriving somewhere new and walking through it slowly, taking far too many photographs along the way. I travel every chance I get, and the entire feeling of it, the planning, the being there, the looking back at it later, is honestly one of the biggest sources of happiness in my life.

So instead of a portfolio of decks, here are seven things that made me happy on a trip I took a couple of months ago, and a little about what each one taught me about my own eye.

On Vibrance

Vibrant is not the loudest colour on the page. It is the one that makes someone stop scrolling.

Every photo above is really just proof of a small, deliberate choice. A caption, a crop, a moment I decided was worth keeping. I think that is what a brand actually is too. Not one big campaign, but hundreds of tiny honest decisions, made often enough that people start to recognise the feeling before they even recognise the logo.

And since we are here, entry one is my suitcase falling apart on a bus in Galle, and entry two is the day I hurt my shoulder and my partner ended up carrying both our suitcases and his own backpack because we simply did not have the right bag between us. So if you are looking for someone who already thinks about how a brand shows up in someone's hands on the most inconvenient day, on the way somewhere good, I would love to talk.
